record.original_question: Given a proportionally modular numerical semigroup by its minimal generators, find formulas for its Frobenius number, genus, and type directly from that minimal generating system.

evidence.quote: The question of giving formulas for the Frobenius number, genus and type of a proportionally modular numerical semigroup in terms of its system of minimal generators remains unsolved too.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement in $\mathbb{N}$. The Frobenius number $F(S)$ is the largest integer not in $S$, the genus $g(S)$ is the cardinality of $\mathbb{N}\setminus S$, and the type $t(S)$ is the cardinality of the set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers $\{x\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus S : x+s\in S\text{ for all }s\in S\setminus\{0\}\}$. Every numerical semigroup admits a unique minimal system of generators $\{n_1<n_2<\cdots<n_e\}$.

A numerical semigroup $S$ is called proportionally modular if there exist positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ with $c\le a$ such that
$$S=\{x\in\mathbb{N} : ax \bmod b \le cx\}.$$

Problem: Given a proportionally modular numerical semigroup $S$ specified by its minimal system of generators $\{n_1,\dots,n_e\}$, provide explicit closed-form formulas, expressed solely in terms of $n_1,\dots,n_e$, for each of the three invariants $F(S)$, $g(S)$, and $t(S)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches confirm that, although proportionally modular numerical semigroups have been characterized in terms of their minimal generators, no closed-form formulas for the Frobenius number, genus, or type in terms of the minimal generating system are known. The broader Frobenius problem is open for embedding dimension ≥ 3, and the proportionally modular case remains an open subproblem.

status_evidence.title: The Frobenius problem for numerical semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Frobenius problem solved for embedding dimension 2 and open for embedding dimension ≥ 3 in general.
status_evidence.claim: Underlying Frobenius problem remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: The genus, the Frobenius number, and the pseudo-Frobenius numbers
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses genus, Frobenius and pseudo-Frobenius for special families.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area; no general formulas for proportionally modular case.
